hypothesis: A comparison harness with an analytic tolerance policy separates legitimate reduction-order and precision differences from faults larger than the policy bound plus the candidate's own deviation; faults up to about the bound can escape. Exercised CPU-against-CPU because no GPU is present.
input_data: orders: sequential, pairwise tree, 32-lane blocked (sequential lanes then tree); precisions float64 and float32
exact dot products by TwoProduct + math.fsum
all 131072 single dropped products per policy
mathematical_model: For a sum of terms each passing through k roundings, |computed - exact| <= gamma_k * sum|a_j x_j| with gamma_k = k u/(1 - k u), u = 2^-53 (float64) or 2^-24 (float32, inputs rounded). The policy tolerance for two outputs is the sum of their bounds; bitwise mode compares bit patterns. A dropped term p is detected when |p| > tolerance + |candidate - reference| (triangle inequality); smaller faults may escape.
numerical_result: 123/128 rows differ bitwise between float64 orders; max difference/bound 0.00173; float32 violates the float64 policy on 128 rows and stays at 0.00874 of its own bound; single dropped products undetected: 0/131072 (float64 policy), 708/131072 (float32 policy, largest missed |a_j x_j| 0.000589 against row tolerance 0.000594; undetected above the row bound: 0 (float64), 1 (float32, ratio 1.00016)). GPU present: False (no GPU kernel was run).
observation_model: Elementwise absolute differences, bitwise equality and ratios to the policy bound.
